entries.title: Numbers 14:1
segments: A long course of bondange, whether bodily or spiritual, is suited to produce a weak and cowardly spirit; to degrade and debase the human mind, and unfit it for great and noble deeds.

entries.title: Numbers 14:5
segments: Fell on their faces; as a sign of their deep grief for the sin of the people, and their earnest intercession with God in their behalf.

entries.title: Numbers 14:6
segments: Rent their clothes; thus they expressed deep sorrow and holy indignation for the unbelieving and rebellious spirit of the people.

entries.title: Numbers 14:9
segments: Are bread for us; food for our swords.  Compare

. 
 
Rebellion against God is the great cause of human sorrow.  By trusting in him and doing his will, men may obtain all needed blessings, in the best way, at the right time, and with only those sacrifices which will in the end promote their highest good.

entries.title: Numbers 14:10
segments: The most unreasonable men are most ready to use mob violence.  Instead of answering their opponents, they attempt to kill them.  Sometimes they for a time succeed, but often they bring ruin on themselves.

entries.title: Numbers 14:11
segments: Men may see the most stupendous miracles, and receive the greatest temporal mercies, and yet remain enemies to God.  No means, without the converting influences of his Spirit, will ever lead them to love and serve him.

entries.title: Numbers 14:16
segments:
Therefore he hath slain them; this, Moses thought, would be greatly to God's dishonor. 
 
Good men dread what will dishonor God more than any temporal evils, and desire the promotion of his glory more than the reception of all temporal mercies.

entries.title: Numbers 14:17
segments: Let the power of my Lord be great; be greatly manifested in forgiving their iniquity, and bringing them into the land of promise.

entries.title: Numbers 14:20
segments: According to thy word; God so far hearkened to Moses as to spare the people for a time, and to bring their children into the promised land.
The righteous are foten the means of averting great calamities from the wicked, and bringing upon them unspeakable good.

entries.title: Numbers 14:21
segments:
But as truly as I live--filled with the glory of the Lord; though Jehovah, upon the intercession of Moses, would spare the people from immediate destruction, he would yet deal with them in such a way as to manifest to all the earth his glorious attributes, mingling justice with mercy. 
 
God will bestow mercy only in such a way as is consistent with justice, wisdom, goodness, and truth--only in such a way as will glorify himself, give a correct view of his character, and fill the hearts of all holy beings with admiration and delight.

entries.title: Numbers 14:22
segments: Ten times; that is, often, a definite number for an indefinite.

entries.title: Numbers 14:24
segments: Steadfastness in duty, however unpopular or dangerous, is the way to glory, honor, and blessedness.

entries.title: Numbers 14:25
segments: Dwelt in the valley; probably the valley at the foot of the hill mentioned
, whence they could easily take possession of the hill-top.
These words are inserted by Moses in a parenthetical way, to explain the reason of the command that follows.

entries.title: Numbers 14:28
segments: God sometimes takes men at their word, and evils which they wickedly imprecate, he in righteous judgment brings upon them.

entries.title: Numbers 14:31
segments: Ye said;

entries.title: Numbers 14:33
segments: Bear your whoredoms; suffer the effects of their sins.
Apostasy from God is spiritual whoredom.

Forty years; from the time they left Egypt. 
 
Many evils come upon children in consequence of the sins of parents; but, if they do not imitate their parents; but, if they do not imitate their parents, nor disobey God, he will overrule these evils for their highest good.

entries.title: Numbers 14:34
segments: Know my breach of promise; or my turning away from you; that is, experience its bitter effects in your destruction.

entries.title: Numbers 14:38
segments: In due time, all will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

entries.title: Numbers 14:39
segments: These sayings; what God had told him.

entries.title: Numbers 14:40
segments: The mountain; which lies north-west of Kadesh.

entries.title: Numbers 14:41
segments: As the Lord never brings evils upon any but for the wisest and best reasons, when he does bring them, none should murmur against him, but all should cheerfully submit, feeling that he afflicts them less than their iniquities deserve, and saying, It is the Lord; let him do as seemeth good in his sight.

entries.title: Numbers 14:45
segments: Hormah; a place in the south part of Canaan, not many miles from Kadesh.  It was before called Zephath.
